meta.title: {brand} — IBS diary: track your symptoms and find your triggers
meta.description: A free IBS symptom diary. Track what you eat, your gut symptoms, your stress and your sleep, and after two weeks see what your symptoms seem to be linked to. No account, and private on your own phone.
meta.ogAlt: {brand}: IBS diary for food, symptoms, stress and sleep

severity.label: How bad?
severity.scale: 0 = no symptoms, 10 = the worst pain you know

bristol.label: Stool (Bristol scale)
bristol.hint: Optional. Type 1 is hard, type 7 is watery.

landing.title: Track your gut symptoms and discover what they're linked to
landing.lead: {brand} is a simple diary for people with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). In a few seconds, you log what you eat, your symptoms, when you feel stressed and how you sleep. After two weeks, you'll see what your symptoms seem to be linked to.

one.title: Log
one.body: Choose Food, Symptom or Stress. The time is already filled in, so an entry takes about ten seconds.

two.title: See your patterns
two.body: After about two weeks, {brand} shows whether your symptoms are mainly linked to food, stress or sleep.

three.title: Discuss it
three.body: Take your overview to your GP or a gastroenterology dietitian. You can also export all your data as a file.

meal.title: Food
meal.body: Your meals and portion sizes, with tags such as onion/garlic, dairy, wheat or legumes.

symptom.title: Symptoms
symptom.body: Abdominal pain, bloating, cramps or diarrhoea, with severity from 0 to 10 and your stool type on the Bristol scale.

stress.title: Stress
stress.body: How tense you are and why, including anxiety beforehand about possible symptoms.

sleep.title: Sleep and day
sleep.body: Your sleep, how much you drink and move, and data from your smartwatch if you like.

landing.aboutBody1: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common bowel condition. Typical symptoms include abdominal pain, bloating, cramps, and diarrhoea or constipation. Symptoms often vary from day to day.
landing.aboutBody2: What triggers symptoms differs from person to person. Certain foods (such as onion, garlic, dairy or wheat), stress and poor sleep can all play a role. The gut and the brain influence each other: tension can make symptoms worse, and symptoms in turn cause tension. A diary helps you map your personal pattern.
landing.aboutMore: Read more about IBS on the NHS website
landing.loopTitle: Stress and gut symptoms reinforce each other
landing.loopBody: Tension can make your gut more restless, and a restless gut causes more tension. Sometimes this starts before anything has happened, for example before a train journey or an appointment. {brand} tracks this ‘stress beforehand’ separately, so you can see the connection.
landing.privacyBody: Everything you enter is stored only on your own phone. There is no account, no server holding your data and no tracker watching. That means we cannot see your data.

privacyPoints.export: Export and erase whenever you want

landing.insightBody: No complicated charts, just a clear summary of what your symptoms seem to be linked to, including how much data it is based on. {brand} shows patterns and never makes a diagnosis.

faq.a1: Tracking and insights are free, with no subscription and no ads. Only the PDF report for your doctor or dietitian costs a small one-off fee, paid with iDEAL.
faq.a2: No. {brand} shows patterns in what you track yourself. Always discuss what you see with your GP or a (gastro) dietitian before changing your diet or lifestyle.
faq.a3: Only in the browser on your own device; nothing is sent to a server. Make a backup now and then via Settings, because clearing your browser data also deletes your diary.
faq.a4: The first patterns appear after about two weeks. The longer and more completely you track, the more reliable the insights.
faq.a5: Yes. After your first visit, you can add {brand} to your phone's home screen. From then on, everything works without an internet connection.
faq.q6: Does this help with the low-FODMAP diet?
faq.a6: {brand} helps you keep track of how you react to certain foods, for example during the reintroduction phase. Ideally, follow a low-FODMAP diet with guidance from a gastroenterology dietitian.

landing.finalBody: Free, with no account, and private on your own phone.
landing.footerDisclaimer: {brand} provides insight into patterns and is not a medical device. It does not diagnose or give treatment advice. If you have persistent or new symptoms, contact your GP.

privacy.title: Privacy, in plain language
privacy.intro: {brand} is built around one promise: what you track about your gut stays yours. Here's exactly what that means.

where.title: Where is my data?
where.body: Everything you enter (meals, symptoms, stress, sleep and notes) is stored in the browser on this device (IndexedDB). It is never sent to us or to anyone else.

account.title: Do I need an account?
account.body: No. There is no account, no email address and no password, so we don't know who you are either.

analytics.title: Do you measure anything?
analytics.body: We only count visits on the public pages (the home page and this privacy statement), anonymously and without cookies (Vercel Web Analytics). We measure nothing at all inside the app, and your health data never ends up in these statistics.

backup.title: What if I lose my phone?
backup.body: Because we don't store your data, we can't restore it either. So make a backup now and then via Settings → Make a backup. {brand} will remind you in good time.

control.title: Can I erase everything?
control.body: Yes. Settings → Erase everything removes all data from this device in one go. Clearing your browser data works too.

medical.title: Not medical advice
medical.body: {brand} shows patterns but does not diagnose or give treatment advice. Discuss what you see with your GP or a (gastro) dietitian.

payment.title: Paying for the report
payment.body: You pay for the PDF report with iDEAL through our payment partner Mollie. Mollie processes your payment details (such as your bank and IBAN) under its own privacy policy. We are only told whether the payment succeeded. Your health data is never included: the report is created on your own device.

s1.title: A diary for your gut
s1.body: Log what you eat, when your gut plays up and when you feel stressed. It only takes a few taps each time.

s2.title: After two weeks, patterns appear
s2.body: {brand} compares your symptoms with what you eat, your stress and your sleep. The more you log, the clearer the picture becomes.

s3.title: Everything stays on this device
s3.body: No account, no server, no trackers. Make a backup now and then, because we can't restore anything for you.

s4.title: Insight, not a diagnosis
s4.body: {brand} shows what seems to be linked. That is not medical advice. Discuss any patterns with your GP or a gastroenterology dietitian before you change anything.

s5.title: What do you want to track?
s5.body: Pick the food tags you use most often; they'll appear at the top. You can change this at any time.
